Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n294\t        return Ok(dt);\n295\t    }\n296\t\n297\t    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n298\t        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n299\t        ts_str\n300\t    )))\n301\t}\n302\t\n303\t/// Base trait for all format parsers\n304\tpub trait FormatParser {\n305\t    /// Parse events from the source\n306\t    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n307\t\n308\t    /// Parse events from the source, starting from a given byte offset for incremental parsing.\n309\t    ///\n310\t    /// For formats that support incremental parsing (JSONL, append-only logs), this allows\n311\t    /// the parser to skip already-processed content and only parse new data.\n312\t    ///\n313\t    /// # Arguments\n314\t    ///\n315\t    /// * `source_path` - Path to the source file\n316\t    /// * `plugin` - Plugin configuration for this source\n317\t    /// * `start_offset` - Byte offset to start reading from (0 for full parse)\n318\t    ///\n319\t    /// # Returns\n320\t    ///\n321\t    /// - `Ok(events)` - Vector of parsed events\n322\t    /// - `Err(_)` - Parse error (check `is_skippable()` for non-fatal errors)\n323\t    fn parse_incremental(\n324\t        &self,\n325\t        source_path: &Path,\n326\t        plugin: &Plugin,\n327\t        start_offset: u64,\n328\t    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n329\t        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n330\t        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n331\t        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n332\t    }\n333\t\n334\t    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n335\t    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n336\t}\n337\t\n338\t/// pub end_offset: u64,\n345\t    pub metadata: Option<Value>,\n346\t    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n347\t    /// is a child of another session)\n348\t    pub parent_session_id: Option<String>,\n349\t}\n350\t\n351\t#[cfg(test)]\n352\tmod tests {\n353\t    use super::*;\n354\t    use serde_json::json;\n355\t\n356\t    #[test]\n357\t    fn Each parser handles one log format:\n//!\n//! - **[`JsonlParser`]**: JSONL format (Claude Code, Codex, Goose)\n//! - **[`MarkdownParser`]**: Markdown format (Aider)\n//! - **[`JsonTreeParser`]**: JSON tree format (OpenCode legacy)\n//! - **[`JsonArrayParser`]**: JSON array format (Gemini CLI)\n//! - **[`SqliteParser`]**: SQLite format (Cursor, Windsurf)\n//!\n//! # When to Use\n//!\n//! These parsers are used internally by the scraper plugin system. Each plugin\n//! specifies its format in the `[source] format` field, and the corresponding\n//! parser is instantiated to normalize events.\n//!\n//! # Parser Behavior\n//!\n//! All parsers:\n//! - Read source files in streaming fashion\n//! - Extract timestamps, roles, content, and metadata\n//! - Normalize to the canonical [`Event`] schema\n//! - Handle errors gracefully usize,\n}\n\nimpl ParseContext {\n    pub fn new(session_id: String, source_agent: String, source_file: String) -> Self {\n        ParseContext {\n            session_id,\n            source_agent,\n            source_file,\n            project: None,\n            model: None,\n            line_number: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn with_project(mut self, project: Returns true if the field name starts with `^`, false otherwise.\n/// Handles empty strings gracefully (returns false).\n///\n/// # Examples\n/// ```\n/// use agentscribe::parser::has_caret_prefix;\n///\n/// assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^foo\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"foo\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"bar^baz\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"\"));\n/// ```\npub fn has_caret_prefix(field_name: &str) -> bool {\n    field_name.starts_with('^')\n}\n\n/// Extract a nested field from JSON using dot notation\npub fn extract_field(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n    if path.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let mut current = value;\n    for part in path.split('.') {\n        // Handle array indexing like parts[0]\n        if let Some(bracket_pos) = part.find('[') {\n            let key = &part[..bracket_pos];\n            let index_str = &part[bracket_pos + 1..part.len() - 1];\n            let index: usize = index_str.parse().ok()?;\n\n            current = current.get(key)?.get(index)?;\n        } else {\n            current = current.get(part)?;\n        }\n    }\n    Some(current.clone())\n}\n\n/// Extract a string field from JSON\npub fn extract_string(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let field = extract_field(value, path)?;\n    match field {\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse timestamp from various formats\npub fn parse_timestamp(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let ts_str = extract_string(value, path)\n        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 first\n    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n            // Milliseconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n        } else {\n            // Seconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n        };\n        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Extract a field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// **Envelope-first with payload fallback for caret-prefixed paths:**\n/// - If path starts with `^`, try envelope first (remove `^` prefix)\n/// - If envelope is None OR field not found in envelope, fallback to payload\n/// - Otherwise, extract from payload only\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `^field`:**\n/// 1. Try `envelope.field` (if envelope exists)\n/// 2. Fallback to `payload.field` (if envelope missing or field not found)\n/// 3. Return None (if both fail)\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `field` (no caret):**\n/// - Extract from `payload.field` only\n///\n/// Supports dot notation for nested fields (e.g., `^outer.ts` or `user.role`)\n/// and array indexing (e.g., `items[0].name`).\npub fn extract_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<Value> {\n    if has_caret_prefix(path) {\n        // Strip the caret prefix\n        if let Some(envelope_path) = path.strip_prefix('^') {\n            // Try envelope first\n            if let Some(env) = envelope {\n                if let Some(value) = extract_field(env, envelope_path) {\n                    return Some(value); // Found in envelope\n                }\n            }\n            // Fallback to payload (using path without ^)\n            extract_field(payload, envelope_path)\n        } else {\n            // Should not happen due to starts_with check, but handle defensively\n            None\n        }\n    } else {\n        // No caret prefix - extract from payload only\n        extract_field(payload, path)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a string field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_with_envelope` that converts the raw `Value` to a string,\n/// following the same coercion rules as `extract_string` (String, Number, Bool, Null).\npub fn extract_string_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    let value = extract_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)?;\n    match value {\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n        Value::Array(arr) => {\n            // Handle content arrays (e.g., Claude Code format with text blocks and tool calls)\n            // Extract text from all text blocks in the array\n            let text_parts: Vec<String> = arr\n                .iter()\n                .filter_map(|item| {\n                    if let Some(obj) = item.as_object() {\n                        // Check for text blocks: {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"...\"}\n                        if obj.get(\"type\").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) == Some(\"text\") {\n                            return obj\n                                .get(\"text\")\n                                .and_then(|t| t.as_str())\n                                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                    None\n                })\n                .collect();\n            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                Some(text_parts.join(\" \"))\n            }\n        }\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a timestamp from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_string_with_envelope` that parses the extracted string\n/// as a timestamp. Supports ISO 8601, Unix epoch (seconds/milliseconds), and\n/// UTC-naive formats.\npub fn parse_timestamp_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let ts_str = extract_string_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)\n        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 first\n    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n            // Milliseconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n        } else {\n            // Seconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n        };\n        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Base trait for all format parsers\npub trait FormatParser {\n    /// Parse events from the source\n    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n\n    /// Parse events from the source, starting from a given byte offset for incremental parsing.\n    ///\n    /// For formats that support incremental parsing (JSONL, append-only logs), this allows\n    /// the parser to skip already-processed content and only parse new data.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `source_path` - Path to the source file\n    /// * `plugin` - Plugin configuration for this source\n    /// * `start_offset` - Byte offset to start reading from (0 for full parse)\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(events)` - Vector of parsed events\n    /// - `Err(_)` - Parse error (check `is_skippable()` for non-fatal errors)\n    fn parse_incremental(\n        &self,\n        source_path: &Path,\n        plugin: &Plugin,\n        start_offset: u64,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n    }\n\n    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n}\n\n/// Information about a detected session\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\npub struct SessionInfo {\n    pub session_id: String,\n    pub start_offset: u64,\n    pub end_offset: u64,\n    pub metadata: Option<Value>,\n    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n    /// is a child of another session)\n    pub parent_session_id: Option<String>,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use serde_json::json;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_extract_field_simple() {\n        let value = json!({\"name\": \"test\", session-specific  \n3. **Unreliable timestamp matching** - Timezone ambiguity and format differences prevent precise correlation\n\n---\n\n## Companion Index Mechanism\n\n### How It Works\n\nAgentScribe's companion index system (`src/scraper/companion.rs`) is designed to correlate companion metadata files with main session logs. It:\n\n- Loads JSONL files containing per-session metadata\n- Keys entries by `thread_id` or `session_id` fields\n- Returns metadata for a given session ID via `CompanionIndex::get(session_id)`\n\n**Expected structure:**\n```json\n{\"thread_id\": \"abc123\", \"model\": \"gpt-4\", \"cwd\": \"/home/user/project\"}\n{\"thread_id\": \"def456\", \"model\": \"gpt-3.5-turbo\", \"cwd\": \"/home/user/other\"}\n```\n\n### Requirements\n\nThe companion index mechanism requires:\n- **Per-session keys:** Each entry must have a `thread_id` or `session_id` field\n- **1:1 mapping:** One metadata record per session\n- **Direct lookup:** Session ID → metadata via hash map lookup\n\n---\n\n## Aider Analytics Structure\n\n### Format\n\nFrom `aider/analytics.py`, each analytics event has:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"event\": \"message_send\",\n  \"properties\": {\n    \"main_model\": \"gpt-4\",\n    \"weak_model\": \"gpt-3.5-turbo\",\n    \"total_tokens\": 1234,\n    \"total_cost\": 0.05\n  },\n  \"user_id\": \"uuid-string-for-user\",\n  \"time\": 1710492000\n}\n```\n\n**Key fields:**\n- `user_id`: Persistent UUID4 identifying the user across ALL sessions\n- `time`: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch, UTC)\n- `properties`: Event metadata (model, tokens, cost)\n\n### What's Missing\n\n**No session identifier exists.** The analytics file contains:\n- `user_id`: Global user identifier (same value in every event)\n- `time`: Event timestamp (not a session ID)\n\nThere is NO field that uniquely identifies a session or can be used as a foreign key to chat history.\n\n---\n\n## AgentScribe Aider Session Detection\n\n### Delimiter-Based Detection\n\nThe Aider plugin uses delimiter-based session detection (`plugins/aider.toml`):\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"delimiter\"\ndelimiter_pattern = \"^# aider chat started at \"\n```\n\n### Session ID Generation\n\nFrom `src/parser/markdown.rs::detect_sessions()`:\n\n1. Split file by delimiter lines: `# aider chat started at 2024-03-15 10:00:00`\n2. Generate session IDs: `{filename}-{session_num}`\n   - Example: `.aider.chat.history.md-0`, `.aider.chat.history.md-1`\n3. Extract timestamp from delimiter (human-readable format)\n\n### Session Metadata\n\n**Delimiter format:**\n```\n# aider chat started at 2024-03-15 10:00:00\n```\n\n**Problems:**\n- No timezone specified (local time? UTC?)\n- Human-readable format (not easily parsed)\n- No session ID or thread ID\n- Timestamp represents session start, not individual events\n\n---\n\n## Correlation Attempts\n\n### 1. Direct Session Key Lookup\n\n**Attempt:** Use `user_id` as session identifier\n\n**Problem:** `user_id` is persistent across ALL sessions. Every analytics event from the same user has the same `user_id`. There is no per-session granularity.\n\n**Result:** ❌ NOT FEASIBLE - Cannot distinguish between sessions\n\n---\n\n### 2. Timestamp Overlap Matching\n\n**Attempt:** Correlate delimiter timestamps with analytics event timestamps\n\n**Problems:**\n\n1. **Timezone ambiguity**\n   - Delimiter: `2024-03-15 10:00:00` (no timezone)\n   - Analytics: `1710492000` (UTC Unix timestamp)\n   - Cannot reliably match without knowing the delimiter's timezone\n\n2. **No 1:1 mapping**\n   - One delimiter = session start\n   - Multiple analytics events per session (each message is an event)\n   - Cannot determine which delimiter corresponds to which event sequence\n\n3. **Timestamp format inconsistency**\n   - Delimiter timestamps are human-readable and potentially inconsistent\n   - Analytics timestamps are precise Unix epochs\n   - Parsing delimiter timestamps is unreliable\n\n4. **Session boundary ambiguity**\n   - Sessions detected by delimiter position in file\n   - Analytics events have independent timestamps\n   - No clear way to map event sequences to delimiter ranges\n\n**Result:** ❌ NOT FEASIBLE - Too much ambiguity for reliable correlation\n\n---\n\n### 3. Hybrid Approach (User ID + Time Window)\n\n**Attempt:** Combine `user_id` with approximate time windows\n\n**Problems:**\n\n1. **User ID adds no value** - Same user ID for all sessions from same user\n2. **Time windows are ambiguous** - Same timezone problems as timestamp overlap\n3. **Multiple sessions could overlap** - Sessions can be concurrent or overlapping in time\n\n**Result:** ❌ NOT FEASIBLE - User ID doesn't reduce ambiguity\n\n---\n\n## Structural Incompatibility Summary\n\n| Aspect | Aider Chat History | Aider Analytics | Compatible? |\n|--------|-------------------|-----------------|--------------|\n| **Session identifier** | Delimiter position | None | ❌ NO |\n| **User identifier** | None | `user_id` (global) | ❌ NO (different scopes) |\n| **Timestamp format** | Human-readable (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`) | Unix epoch (UTC) | ⚠️ AMBIGUOUS |\n| **Timezone** | Not specified | UTC | ❌ NO |\n| **Granularity** | Per session | Per event | ❌ NO |\n| **Count** | 1 record per session | N events per session | ❌ NO |\n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\n### Why Correlation Is Not Feasible\n\n1. **No shared session identifier:** Analytics lacks a field that can be used as a foreign key to chat sessions\n2. **User ID is global, not per-session:** `user_id` identifies the user across all sessions, not individual sessions\n3. **Timestamp matching is unreliable:** Timezone ambiguity, format differences, and lack of 1:1 mapping prevent precise correlation\n4. **Structural mismatch:** Chat history is session-based; analytics is event-based with no session grouping\n\n### Recommendation\n\n**Do NOT wire aider analytics as a companion index.** The data structure is fundamentally incompatible with the companion mechanism's session-based keying requirements.\n\nThe documentation in `plugins/aider.toml` correctly identifies this incompatibility:\n\n```toml\n# Companion index decision (bf-xp9w):\n# Aider analytics JSONL (~/.aider.analytics.jsonl) is NOT wired as a companion_index\n# because it lacks session-level identifiers needed for correlation.\n```\n\n### Alternative Approaches\n\nIf analytics metadata (model, tokens, cost) is needed for aider sessions:\n\n1. **Add session IDs to analytics:** Modify aider to emit a session identifier in analytics events\n2. **Separate metadata file:** Create a companion file that explicitly maps session IDs to metadata\n3. **Post-scrape enrichment:** Use project, timestamp heuristics, or user input to backfill metadata\n\n---\n\n## Related Documentation\n\n- **Full analysis:** `notes/bf-xp9w.md` - aider analytics companion evaluation\n- **Plugin config:** `plugins/aider.toml` - Aider plugin with companion index decision\n- **Companion implementation:** `src/scraper/companion.rs` - Companion index mechanism\n- **Session detection:** `src/parser/markdown.rs` - Delimiter-based session detection\n\n---\n\n**Status:** ✅ Analysis complete - Correlation confirmed as NOT feasible  \n**Next steps:** None - This bead can be closed with documented infeasibility\n","numLines":224,"startLine":1,"totalLines":224}}}
